'''Boštjan''' "'''Boki'''" '''Nachbar''' (born July 3, 1980) is a Slovenian former professional [[basketball]] player. A 2.06 m forward, he spent most of his career between the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and the [[EuroLeague]]. Nachbar helped lead the [[Slovenia national basketball team|Slovenian national basketball team]] to a fourth place at [[EuroBasket 2009]].

==Professional career==

===Europe===
Nachbar started his professional career by joining the [[KK Union Olimpija|Olimpija Ljubljana]] basketball club in the 1997–98 season. He played with Olimpija in Europe's top-level competition the [[EuroLeague]], where he averaged 7 points and 2 rebounds per game. In the 2000–01 season he signed with [[Pallacanestro Treviso|Benetton Treviso]] basketball club, as the youngest [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]] player. With Benetton, he averaged 4 points and grabbed 2 rebounds in the EuroLeague. In the next season, he helped Benetton get to the Final Four of the EuroLeague, as he improved his statistics to 13 points and 4 rebounds per game. In his best game of the season, against [[Idea Slask Wroclaw]], he scored 28 points, hitting 6 three-pointers. He won the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]] championship and the [[Italian Supercup]] in 2002.

===NBA===
Nachbar was selected by the Houston Rockets as the 15th overall pick in the [[2002 NBA draft]]. He played for the Rockets for three seasons, but only averaged about 10 minutes per game. In 2004, he went to the [[New Orleans Pelicans|New Orleans Hornets]], where he averaged about 8 points in 21 minutes per game. During the [[2004–05 NBA season]], he scored 21 points against his former team, the Rockets, which was a career high. In the 2005–06 season, however, he had a difficult time getting off the bench once again was traded to the [[New Jersey Nets]] just before the trading deadline in exchange for [[Marc Jackson]], [[Linton Johnson]], and cash considerations. He had a great season with New Jersey as the team's 6th man, making many contributions to the club before they lost in the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] semis to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].

Nachbar's final NBA game was played on April 16, 2008, in a 94–105 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]] where he recorded 11 points, 1 assist and 1 block.

===Return to Europe===
On July 20, 2008, Nachbar returned to Europe when he signed a 3-year [[Euro|€]]9.6 million euros [[net income]] contract with the [[Russian Basketball Super League 1|Russian Superleague]] club [[MBC Dynamo Moscow|Dynamo Moscow]],<ref>[http://www.siol.net/sportal/kosarka/2008/07/sanjski_prestop_nachbarja_v_moskvo.aspx Sanjski prestop Nachbarja v Moskvo] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019093457/http://www.siol.net/sportal/kosarka/2008/07/sanjski_prestop_nachbarja_v_moskvo.aspx |date=October 19, 2013 }} {{in lang|sl}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3497994 |title=Ex-Nets F Nachbar, Dynamo Moscow agree to 3-year, $14.3M deal |access-date=July 17, 2024 |archive-date=February 28, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240228133944/https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3497994 |url-status=live }}</ref> giving him one of the most expensive contracts in European pro basketball history. The contract also included opt out clauses after each season. He averaged 16.1 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.2 assists, and 1.4 steals in [[European professional club basketball system|Europe's second-level competition]], the [[ULEB Eurocup|EuroCup]], during the 2008–09 season.<ref>[https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/game-center/?seasoncode=U2008&pcode=AHX&clubcode=dyn Eurocup 2008-09 season.]</ref>

Nachbar opted out of his contract with Dynamo Moscow on May 17, 2009. In July 2009, he signed a 2-year contract with a team option for the second year with the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish League]] club [[Efes Pilsen S.K.|Efes Pilsen]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europa/euroleague/3465/nachbar_inks_for_efes_pilsen.html |title=Sportando.net Nachbar inks for Efes Pilsen - The Slovenian to stay in Europe. |access-date=July 14, 2009 |archive-date=October 19, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019055540/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europa/euroleague/3465/nachbar_inks_for_efes_pilsen.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/55170/efes-pilsen-lands-forward-bostjan-nachbar Efes Pilsen lands forward Bostjan Nachbar]</ref> He averaged 6.7 points and 1.9 rebounds per game in the EuroLeague in the [[2009-10 Euroleague|2009-10 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=AHX&seasoncode=E2009 |title=Euroleague.net - 2009-10 season. |access-date=February 10, 2015 |archive-date=February 10, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210181518/http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=AHX&seasoncode=E2009 |url-status=live }}</ref> In his second year with Efes, Nachbar improved his stats in the EuroLeague to 8.3 points and 2.8 rebounds. On June 24, 2011, Nachbar announced via Twitter that he won't stay for a third season with the team.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/turkey/28741/bostjan-nachbar-leaves-efes-istanbul.html |title=Bostjan Nachbar leaves Efes Istanbul |access-date=November 30, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203003626/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/turkey/28741/bostjan-nachbar-leaves-efes-istanbul.html |archive-date=December 3, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Nachbar started the 2011–12 season out due to an ankle injury. After recovering from the injury, he was mentioned as a potential reinforcement for several NBA teams.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/usa/nba/33473/knicks-seeking-34-swingman-for-bench.html |title=Knicks Seeking 3/4 Swingman For Bench |access-date=November 30, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203001813/http://www.sportando.net/eng/usa/nba/33473/knicks-seeking-34-swingman-for-bench.html |archive-date=December 3, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/usa/nba/33719/charlotte-bobcats-plan-to-audition-bostjan-nachbar-and-jamario-moon.html |title=Charlotte Bobcats plan to audition Bostjan Nachbar and Jamario Moon |access-date=November 30, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203002522/http://www.sportando.net/eng/usa/nba/33719/charlotte-bobcats-plan-to-audition-bostjan-nachbar-and-jamario-moon.html |archive-date=December 3, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> After not getting a contract in the NBA, Nachbar signed with [[Russian Professional Basketball League|Russian League]] team [[UNICS Kazan]] in January 2012, until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/92512/unics-brings-in-bostjan-nachbar |title=Unics brings in Bostjan Nachbar |access-date=February 10, 2015 |archive-date=September 25, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925043407/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/92512/unics-brings-in-bostjan-nachbar |url-status=live }}</ref> He wasn't able to perform well in UNICS, averaging only 3.1 [[Points per game|PPG]] in the Russian league.

He joined [[Brose Baskets Bamberg]] in July 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/99024/180/brose-baskets-lands-nachbar |title=Brose Baskets lands Nachbar |access-date=August 1, 2012 |archive-date=October 19, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019102747/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/99024/180/brose-baskets-lands-nachbar |url-status=live }}</ref> He had a successful season, leading the team to the [[2012-13 Euroleague|EuroLeague Top 16]], finishing as EuroLeague's second best scorer with 16.1 points per game. He also helped the team regain their [[Basketball Bundesliga]] title, as they won 3–0 in the finals series against [[EWE Baskets Oldenburg]].

On July 23, 2013, Nachbar signed a two-year deal with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite web|title=FC Barcelona announced Bostjan Nachbar|work=Sportando|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/104052/fc-barcelona-announced-bostjan-nachbar.html|publisher=Sportando.net|access-date=July 23, 2013|archive-date=February 10, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210181346/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/104052/fc-barcelona-announced-bostjan-nachbar.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On August 18, 2015, he signed a one-year deal with [[Baloncesto Sevilla]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/173123/baloncesto-sevilla-lands-bostjan-nachbar.html |title=Baloncesto Sevilla lands Bostjan Nachbar |access-date=August 19, 2015 |archive-date=October 14, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171014002948/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/173123/baloncesto-sevilla-lands-bostjan-nachbar.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

On May 14, 2018, Nachbar announced his retirement.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bostjan Nachbar retires at 37|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/spain/acb/274016/bostjan-nachbar-retires-at-37.html|website=Sportando|access-date=May 14, 2018|date=May 14, 2018}}{{Dead link|date=October 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:Boštjan Nachbar 2009.jpg|thumb|upright=0.6|Nachbar with Slovenia at [[EuroBasket 2009]]]]
Nachbar was a member of the senior [[Slovenia national basketball team|Slovenian national team]]. He participated at [[EuroBasket 2003]], [[EuroBasket 2005]], [[EuroBasket 2009]] and [[EuroBasket 2013]]. During the 2005 FIBA EuroBasket, he averaged 11 points and 5 rebounds per game. He was also a member of Slovenia's national team that played at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]] in Japan.

He was also a member of Slovenia's national team that played at the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]] in Turkey. [[EuroBasket 2013]], which took place in his homeland of Slovenia, was his last one before his retirement from the national team.

==Post-playing career==
Nachbar was hired as an international scout by the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bostjan Nachbar to work with the Pistons as an international scout|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/249023/bostjan-nachbar-to-work-with-the-pistons-as-an-international-scout.html|website=sportando.com}}{{Dead link|date=June 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Together with [[Anže Tomić]] and [[Boštjan Gorenc]] he runs the podcast Podrobnosti (eng. Details).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://apparatus.si/oddaja/podrobnosti/|title=Podrobnosti|website=apparatus.si|language=en-US|access-date=March 10, 2018|archive-date=March 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180310201821/https://apparatus.si/oddaja/podrobnosti/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He is married <ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/All_Access_Online_Bostjan_Nachbar_Q_A.html |title=Nachbar talks about wife and season with the NETS |access-date=December 17, 2010 |archive-date=October 26, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131026221315/http://www.nba.com/nets/news/All_Access_Online_Bostjan_Nachbar_Q_A.html |url-status=live }}</ref> and has two daughters, Tara and Ajda.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20130926083748/http://kosarka.si/cestitke-bostjan-nachbar-postal-ocka/ Boštjan Nachbar postal očka] {{in lang|sl}}</ref> His younger brother Grega is assistant coach of [[Premier A Slovenian Basketball League]] club [[Helios Suns]].
